papers.title: The Genetics of Sleep Regulation in Mice.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes forward- and reverse-genetic mouse studies linking specific genes and circuits to vigilance-state dynamics, highlighting phosphorylation-centered control of NREM sleep via the SIK3-HDAC4 pathway and related kinase-phosphatase networks. It also discusses neuromodulator, ion channel, astrocyte, and microglia contributions and methodological constraints in mouse sleep phenotyping.

papers.title: Propofol rapidly reverses cognitive impairments with restoration of sleep stability and alleviation of neuroinflammation in sleep-deprived mice.
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, a single subanesthetic propofol bolus rapidly reversed cognitive impairments (from one hour and persisting 24 hours) while zolpidem was ineffective, and propofol restored NREM sleep stability by increasing medium-to-long NREM episodes. Propofol also upregulated BMAL1, reduced IL-1β and TNF-α, restored BDNF/PSD-95/SYN, and reversed hippocampal dendritic spine loss.

papers.title: Transcranial temporal interference stimulation increases slow waves during human NREM sleep
papers.summary: In 32 participants receiving 1 Hz transcranial temporal interference stimulation (tTIS) to the left insula/ventromedial prefrontal cortex during NREM sleep, tTIS increased slow-wave density by ~20% during and ~30% after stimulation versus a carrier-only control, with a stronger modeled field associated with greater shift toward N3 sleep. Source reconstruction and individualized field modeling showed waves involved more cortex without changed origins.

papers.title: Does recovery sleep structure influence cognitive performance in healthy sleep deprived individuals? A scoping review.
papers.summary: This PRISMA-guided scoping review of 31 studies examined links between recovery sleep structure and cognitive restoration in sleep-deprived healthy adults, finding total sleep time the most important factor for cognitive recovery, with recovery also depending on recent sleep history. Slow-wave activity and sleep microstructure may explain interindividual differences, though most associations relied on group-level rather than interindividual correlations.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into state-dependent synchronization of neural activity by weak tACS fields
papers.summary: Simulating weak tACS in a detailed cortical column model across REM-like and NREM-like network states, stimulation entrained network activity at realistic field strengths despite minimal effects on firing rates. Entrainment was initiated by pyramidal cell entrainment recruiting interneurons state-dependently, with stronger locking in the NREM-like state, and recurrent connectivity was not required for or amplifying entrainment.

papers.title: Evidence for correlated evolution of sleep architecture in chronotype populations of Drosophila melanogaster created by artificial selection
papers.summary: Using artificially selected early and late eclosion chronotype populations of Drosophila melanogaster, the authors found correlated evolution of sleep architecture: early chronotype flies showed greater sleep fragmentation and shorter nighttime sleep latency, while late flies showed weaker changes. Environmental temperature cycles and light intensity modulated sleep timing, and recovery after sleep disruption and simulated jetlag differed between chronotypes.

papers.title: Simultaneous Two-Photon Calcium Imaging, Electroencephalography, and Electromyography with Intracortical Electrical Stimulation in Freely Moving Mice.
papers.summary: This protocol describes an integrated chronic preparation for simultaneous two-photon calcium imaging, intracortical electrical stimulation, EEG, and EMG in freely moving tethered mice, using the retrosplenial cortex as an example target. It yields cellular-resolution calcium signals with concurrent electrophysiological and motor-state measurements and supports repeated optical access and stimulation-aligned analysis.

papers.title: Sleep as a window into thalamocortical pathology: generative modeling implicates NMDA receptor hypofunction in 22q11.2 deletion syndrome.
authors: Marianne B M van den Bree
papers.summary: Applying a conductance-based thalamocortical Dynamic Causal Model to sleep-wake EEG from children with 22q11.2 deletion syndrome (n=28) and siblings (n=17), this study found that increasing NMDA receptor efficacy produced the strongest alignment with sibling spectra (effect sizes 0.32 light NREM, 0.45 deep NREM). Findings implicate NMDA receptor hypofunction as a key thalamocortical mechanism and treatment target in 22q11.2DS.

papers.title: Cross-domain competition for memory reactivation resources during sleep
papers.summary: In a within-subject nap study with 24 participants, targeted memory reactivation cues for an object sequence task during NREM sleep did not indirectly enhance a linked motor task and disrupted object memory consolidation. EEG showed slow oscillation and spindle activity preferentially allocated to the motor trace, suggesting cross-domain memories sharing a common structure compete for reactivation resources.

papers.title: Cycle-based neurostimulation for control of circadian brain network dynamics in human epilepsy
papers.summary: Using longitudinal electrocorticography from individuals with bitemporal epilepsy, the authors found that alignment of circadian hippocampal connectivity rhythms between left and right hippocampus predicts seizure reduction to responsive neurostimulation, and stimulation timing predicts evolution of these rhythms. A nonlinear Kuramoto oscillator model showed in silico optimization of stimulation timing can improve predicted circadian network alignment.

papers.title: Integrating convolutional variational autoencoders and the Gaussian mixture model for efficient manifold learning and clustering of spatially preserved EEG topographic maps.
papers.summary: The authors designed Conv-VaDE, a convolutional variational deep embedding model that places a Gaussian mixture model prior on the latent space of a convolutional VAE with polarity-invariant mechanisms, for clustering EEG microstate topographic maps. Evaluated on 203 eyes-closed healthy participants from the LEMON dataset, Conv-VaDE showed highly reproducible latent geometry (silhouette 0.232 with narrow cross-subject IQR) and a modal K=4 in a rank-based meta-criterion (39.4% vs 29.6% for ModKMeans), while ModKMeans retained higher silhouette and 4-5 percentage points higher Global Explained Variance within the classical cluster-validity register.

papers.title: EEG Source Localization with High-Resolution 40-Tissue Head Models: A Comparative Study with MEG during Photic Driving
papers.summary: This paper presents a BEM-FMM pipeline for EEG source localization using individualized 40-tissue high-resolution head models, computing TES solutions reciprocally to obtain leadfields at roughly 4.5 min per EEG channel on a single workstation. In six participants during photic driving, 40-tissue and 5-layer models produced highly consistent localizations (weighted relative difference below 3%), both closely agreeing with simultaneous MEG localizations in visual cortex.

papers.title: Phosphorylation-dependent ATPase activity regulates subunit shuffling dynamics in cyanobacterial circadian clock proteins.
papers.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
papers.summary: Combining chromatography and single-molecule fluorescence, the authors show that ATPase activity is essential for monomer shuffling in the KaiC hexamer; quantitative modeling indicates that ATP hydrolysis at two monomer-monomer interfaces disassembles hexamers into oligomers that can exchange subunits, and that phosphorylation of the KaiC-CII domain modulates shuffling by affecting nucleotide exchange in the CI domain.

papers.title: Effect of Intraindividual Variability in Sleep on Long-Term Memory Encoding in Sleep-Restricted Individuals.
papers.summary: In a sleep-restriction study with 44 participants, a variable short sleep schedule (8-4-8-4-6 h time-in-bed) led to poorer declarative memory encoding than a control schedule, evidenced by more 'unsure' responses at retrieval, whereas a stable short sleep schedule did not impair memory and increased correct rejections.

papers.title: Capacity-controlled EEG denoising: diminishing reconstruction returns on semi-synthetic benchmarks and task-dependent downstream utility.
papers.summary: The authors evaluated capacity effects and downstream utility of a depthwise-separable EEG denoiser across semi-synthetic benchmarks and BCI/sleep tasks, finding that reconstruction fidelity improvements did not consistently translate to downstream performance: denoising reduced motor imagery accuracy for several artifact types and lowered sleep-stage balanced accuracy, indicating that reconstruction metrics are not universal surrogate endpoints.

papers.title: Environmental enrichment enhances hepatic oxidative stress and antioxidant defenses without modulating immunometabolic gene expression in adult male mice.
papers.summary: In male C57BL/6 mice, six weeks of environmental enrichment lowered hepatic NAD⁺ and raised NADH, reduced lipid peroxidation and protein carbonylation, and increased antioxidant enzyme activities, GSH/GSSG ratio, and sulfhydryl content, while immunometabolic gene expression was unchanged. The findings suggest short-term enrichment optimizes hepatic redox balance without detectable transcriptional changes.

papers.title: A post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification.
papers.summary: The authors propose a post-training quantization framework for EEG-based sleep stage classification that uses layer-wise sensitivity to preserve abnormal weights at original precision while compressing others to 4 bits, plus dynamic low-rank compensation; on Sleep-EDF-20, Sleep-EDF-78, and SHHS, accuracy dropped by less than 1% for most models while model size was reduced nearly 8-fold.

papers.title: Performance evaluation of smart ring-derived sleep parameters compared with portable electroencephalography in university students.
papers.summary: In 49 university students monitored simultaneously with a smart ring and portable EEG at home, the smart ring showed strong correlation for total sleep time (ρ=0.70) but underestimated TST and light sleep, overestimated WASO and deep sleep, and achieved only 50.0% accuracy (κ=0.27) for four-stage sleep classification, indicating limited validity for wake detection and sleep staging.

papers.title: Liraglutide Realigns Corneal Circadian Output Programs and Ameliorates Ocular Surface Abnormalities Under High-Fat-Diet-Induced Metabolic Stress.
papers.summary: In high-fat-diet-fed male C57BL/6J mice, HFD increased corneal rhythmic transcripts (2040 to 3582), delayed mean peak phase, and reduced phase coherence, while liraglutide shifted these toward normal-chow patterns and was associated with improved epithelial ZO-1/occludin, corneal nerve density, mechanical sensitivity, and reduced neutrophil and γδ T-cell accumulation. Canonical core-clock gene parameters showed comparatively limited changes.

papers.title: 'Therapeutic potential of resveratrol against REM sleep deprivation-induced memory deficits: involvement of hippocampal BDNF and TrkB protein expression.
papers.summary: In rats subjected to 6 h daily REM sleep deprivation for four days, resveratrol (40 mg/kg pre-treatment or 10–40 mg/kg post-treatment) attenuated fear-memory deficits (reduced freezing, increased freezing latency) and restored REM-SD-induced reductions in hippocampal BDNF and TrkB protein expression toward control levels.

papers.title: Diurnal Variation in Human Breast Milk: Multi-Omic Characterization and Implications for Infant Circadian Development.
papers.summary: In a cross-sectional study of 89 mother-infant dyads plus paired noon/midnight breast milk samples from 20 lactating women, the authors characterized diurnal multi-omic variation in milk. They identified 20 bacterial genera differing by sampling time and reported midnight enrichment of specific taxa and lipid/amino acid metabolism pathways, suggesting potential implications for infant circadian development.

papers.title: Impact of circadian rhythm disruptions on the emotional brain: gray matter and functional connectivity changes in the amygdala.
papers.summary: This longitudinal 7 T MRI study found that 15 days of experimentally induced circadian rhythm disruption reduced gray matter volume in the left amygdala and its centromedial, laterobasal, and superficial subregions, with no significant right-amygdala changes. Left amygdala volume reductions correlated with worsening Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index scores, and left mPFC–centromedial amygdala connectivity showed a near-significant decrease.

papers.title: Individual deviation network analysis and rat multiomics profiling link sleep deprivation to depressive-like behavior and microbiome-metabolome remodeling.
papers.summary: Combining an individual deviation network analysis in 14,769 NHANES adults with a 21-day rat sleep deprivation model, the study identified Sleep × Depression as the dominant clinical deviation axis. In rats, sleep deprivation produced depressive-like behavior, inflammation, altered colonic tight junction proteins, and microbiome-metabolome remodeling, with module M06 hub metabolites proposed as candidate fecal biomarkers.

papers.title: Implementation of nurse-led frontal electroencephalography for early neurological assessment in patients after cardiac arrest: the FRONT study.
papers.summary: The FRONT hybrid implementation study trained ICU nurses to apply a 6-electrode frontal EEG configuration within 3 h of ICU admission after cardiac arrest. Frontal EEG was applied in 88% of 60 patients (73% within 3 h), with median application time of 20 min and correct electrode placement confirmed in all evaluated patients, supporting nurse-led adoption, acceptability, and fidelity.

papers.title: Sea-Level Polysomnography and Periodic Breathing During Acute Normobaric Hypoxia in Healthy Adults: An Exploratory Study.
papers.summary: In this exploratory study, 54 healthy adults underwent sea-level polysomnography and repeat polysomnography under acute normobaric hypoxia simulating ~3500 m; 11 participants developed sleep-disordered breathing with periodic breathing. Sea-level oxygen desaturation index was independently associated with hypoxic periodic breathing (AUC 0.798; cutoff 1.15 events/h: sensitivity 81.8%, specificity 79.1%).

papers.title: Preprocessing and feature extraction co-optimization for low-power EEG-based neurodegenerative disease detection: a benchmark on STM32 embedded platforms.
papers.summary: Developed a lightweight TinyML framework for EEG-based classification of Alzheimer's disease and frontotemporal dementia on STM32 microcontrollers, evaluating 12 preprocessing techniques and 6 classifiers on 88 participants. Sparse Decomposition combined with XGBoost achieved the best performance with 94.46% accuracy and 92.1% sensitivity while requiring only 45 KB SRAM.

papers.title: Warmer night-time temperatures are linked to poorer associative memory performance.
papers.summary: Examined associations between daily ambient temperatures and cognitive performance in 1,873 midlife and older adults, finding that higher minimum (night-time) temperature was specifically associated with poorer associative memory performance on the Paired Associates task, but not with other cognitive domains.

papers.title: Affective responses during five days of dexmedetomidine-assisted cold-sleep for long-duration spaceflight.
papers.summary: In a small study of six healthy volunteers (five receiving intervention) during a five-day dexmedetomidine-assisted cold-sleep protocol, mixed-effects modeling of daily PANAS scores showed no significant day effect for affective valence or arousal, and no major adverse affective outcomes or recovery rebound were observed.

papers.title: Condition-associated EEG signatures in N-back tasks: temporal dynamics, classification, and generalization.
papers.summary: Investigated EEG signatures of mental workload in 15 adults during two N-back paradigms using an 8-channel setup, finding modest and context-dependent classification performance with distinct spectral and ERP patterns for N-level versus speed manipulations, and limited cross-paradigm generalization.

papers.title: Quality of life impairment in Parkinson's disease with probable REM sleep behavior disorder is primarily linked to fear of falling and anxiety.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cross-sectional study of 468 Parkinson's disease patients, probable REM sleep behavior disorder was associated with worse quality of life, but mediation analyses indicated this relationship was largely indirect, with fear of falling and anxiety accounting for much of it rather than pRBD acting as an independent predictor.

papers.title: Natural Antioxidants in Sleep Deprivation: Mechanisms, Therapeutic Potential, and Future Perspectives.
papers.summary: Reviewed evidence on natural antioxidant compounds and plant extracts as protective interventions against sleep deprivation-induced oxidative stress and inflammation, highlighting their pleiotropic mechanisms but calling for further mechanistic and clinical studies.

papers.title: Adaptation and Validation of the Turkish Version of the Youth Self-Rated Insomnia Scale in an Adolescent Psychiatric Sample.
papers.summary: Adapted and validated the Turkish version of the Youth Self-Rated Insomnia Scale in 83 adolescents with psychiatric disorders, demonstrating excellent internal consistency (Cronbach's α = 0.884), strong test-retest reliability (ICC = 0.89), and a two-factor structure explaining 71.8% of variance.

papers.title: Integrating Inflammation, Pathway Modulation, and Circadian Clock Genes: Conventional and Phytochemical Strategies for Safer Osteoporosis Therapy.
papers.summary: This review discusses integrating circadian biology with conventional and phytochemical therapies for osteoporosis, highlighting that time-sensitive administration aligned with circadian rhythms may improve efficacy and reduce side effects. It reports that phytochemicals such as resveratrol, icariin, genistein, quercetin, and baicalein show osteoprotective effects via antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and modulation of RANKL/OPG, AMPK/SIRT1, ESR, NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin pathways.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnea may exacerbate periodontitis via microbial dysbiosis: A preliminary translational exploratory study.
papers.summary: This translational study combined clinical 16S rRNA sequencing and metabolomics of gingival crevicular fluid in periodontitis patients with and without OSA with a rat model of chronic intermittent hypoxia plus ligature-induced periodontitis. OSA was associated with higher microbial richness, enrichment of Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium, glycerophospholipid-related metabolic differences, and, in rats, greater alveolar bone loss and inflammation, supporting a role for intermittent hypoxia and microbial dysbiosis in exacerbating periodontitis.

papers.title: Longitudinal ACC Alterations with Low-Dose Pregabalin in pBMS.
papers.summary: In a single-arm prospective longitudinal study of 38 moderate-to-severe primary burning mouth syndrome patients and 31 controls, low-dose pregabalin for 4 weeks reduced mean VAS by 3.28 points (ITT), with 44.74% achieving ≥50% pain relief. Baseline ACC Glx/Cr and tNAA/Cr were elevated and correlated with pain/sleep measures, and ACC Glx/Cr decreased after treatment alongside increased pgACC-centered connectivity, while gray matter deficits did not change.

papers.title: The potential mediating role of social frailty in the associations of cognitive function, sleep duration, and life satisfaction with depressive symptoms in older adults: a cross-sectional study using CHARLS data.
papers.summary: Using CHARLS data from 4,491 older adults, this cross-sectional study found that life satisfaction, cognitive function, sleep duration, and social frailty were significantly associated with depressive symptoms, collectively explaining 28.7% of variance. Path analysis indicated that social frailty partially mediates the associations of life satisfaction, cognitive function, and sleep duration with depressive symptoms.

papers.title: Pathological mechanisms of the "lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine" crosstalk network in ectopic fat deposition and skeletal muscle decline.
papers.summary: This review constructs a mechanistic network of 'lifestyle-immunometabolic-neuroendocrine' crosstalk linking unhealthy lifestyle stressors to chronic low-grade inflammation, ectopic fat deposition, and skeletal muscle decline. It proposes that immunometabolic reprogramming and neuroendocrine axis decline act as core drivers amplifying tissue microenvironment remodeling and body composition imbalance.

papers.title: Interrater agreement of seizure onset and spread in scalp EEG
papers.summary: Three board-certified epileptologists independently annotated onset and contralateral spread in 79 scalp EEG seizures from 48 presurgical patients, finding substantial agreement on onset laterality (Gwet k=0.73) and spread presence (0.63) but lower channel-level agreement for spread (Cohen k=0.38) than onset (0.57). Onset timing was more consistent (median MAD 0.40 s) than spread timing (1.99 s), supporting feasibility of scalp EEG spread as a noninvasive marker.

papers.title: Evidence appraisal of clinical practice guidelines for managing menopausal symptoms: a systematic literature review.
papers.summary: This systematic review appraised 13 U.S. clinical practice guidelines for managing menopausal symptoms and found variable quality, with none rated high quality and no guideline providing decision-support tools or therapeutic sequencing algorithms for nonhormone therapy selection. It highlights the need for structured decision frameworks to guide therapy based on contraindications, patient preferences, and risk profiles.

papers.title: Filgotinib Safety Profile: A Pharmacovigilance Study Using Data from the VigiBase and Food and Drug Administration Adverse Event Reporting System.
papers.summary: A pharmacovigilance disproportionality analysis of filgotinib using VigiBase (2207 reports) and FAERS (190 reports) from 2017 to 2025 identified strong signals for lower respiratory tract infection and hypercholesterolemia in VigiBase and for epididymitis and sleep apnea syndrome in FAERS, with median time to onset of 1 month. The findings support continued clinical vigilance for infections, metabolic abnormalities, and testicular-related adverse events.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
